accepted.s:
With reference to the Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It is constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution.
2. It is a quasi-judicial constitutional body.
3. It is constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Article 280 provides for a quasi-judicial Finance Commission constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier.
accepted.tq: Verify the constitutional article, institutional character and periodicity together.

accepted.s: The Finance Commission consists of:
o: A Chairman and four members appointed by the President
A Chairman and three members appointed by Parliament
A Chairman and four members appointed by the Prime Minister
accepted.x: The Finance Commission comprises a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President.
accepted.tq: Test composition and appointing authority in the same question.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the members of the Finance Commission:
1. Their term is specified by the President.
2. They are eligible for reappointment.
3. Their term is fixed permanently by the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The President specifies the term, and members are eligible for reappointment. The Constitution does not permanently prescribe one fixed term.
accepted.tq: Identify the true provisions and reject the absolute claim about a permanently fixed term.

accepted.s: The qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission are prescribed by Parliament under the:
accepted.x: Parliament prescribed the qualifications through the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, also referred to in abbreviated form as the Finance Commission Act, 1951.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact statutory title from plausible but nonexistent titles.

accepted.s: Which of the following is the prescribed qualification for the Chairman of the Finance Commission?
o: Service as a Governor of a State
Experience exclusively as a High Court Chief Justice
Membership of Parliament for ten years
accepted.x: The Chairman must have experience in public affairs.
accepted.tq: Match the office with its exact statutory qualification rather than a prestigious but unstated qualification.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT among the specified fields from which the four members of the Finance Commission are drawn?
o: A person with special knowledge of international diplomacy
A High Court judge or a person qualified to be one
A person with wide experience in financial administration
An expert in government finance and accounts
accepted.x: The specified fields include judicial qualification, government finance and accounts, financial administration, and economics. International diplomacy is not one of them.
accepted.tq: Find the one field outside the statutory list of member qualifications.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the nature of the recommendations of the Finance Commission?
o: They have the force of constitutional amendments.
They are binding on the Union Government in all circumstances.
They are advisory and are not binding.
They are binding only on State Governments.
accepted.x: The recommendations of the Finance Commission are advisory and not binding.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between advisory and binding constitutional recommendations.

accepted.s: P.V. Rajamannar observed that the recommendations of the Finance Commission:
o: Can be modified only by the Supreme Court
May be rejected without assigning any reason
Are automatically enforceable as judicial decrees
Should not be rejected without very compelling reasons
accepted.x: P.V. Rajamannar stated that the recommendations should not be rejected without very compelling reasons.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise qualification attached to the advisory nature of recommendations.

accepted.s: Under Article 281, the President is required to place before each House of Parliament:
o: Only the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General
The recommendations along with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken
The recommendations after approval by the Supreme Court
accepted.x: Article 281 requires the President to lay the Finance Commission’s recommendations together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken before each House of Parliament.
accepted.tq: Test the constitutional procedure and watch for the omission of the explanatory memorandum.

accepted.s: Which Article provides for the Finance Commission, while Article 290 deals with pensions?
accepted.x: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, whereas Article 290 deals with pensions. Article 281 concerns laying the recommendations before Parliament.
accepted.tq: Separate the look-alike constitutional article numbers by their subjects.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly shows the States’ share of central taxes recommended by the 10th to 13th Finance Commissions?
accepted.x: The respective shares were 29% under the 10th, 29.5% under the 11th, 30.5% under the 12th and 32% under the 13th Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Read the sequence across the comparison table without reversing adjacent percentages.

accepted.s: The 10th Finance Commission’s sharing of all central taxes was implemented through the 80th Constitutional Amendment, 2000, with effect from:
accepted.x: The 80th Amendment, 2000 implemented the 10th Finance Commission’s sharing of all central taxes with effect from 1 April 1996.
accepted.tq: Separate the amendment year from its effective date.

accepted.s:
Consider the following sequence of States’ share of central taxes:
1. 42%
2. 41%
3. 41%
This sequence corresponds to the recommendations of the:

accepted.s: The reduction in the States’ share from 42% under the 14th Finance Commission to 41% under the 15th Finance Commission was attributed to:
o: The abolition of the divisible pool
The introduction of the GDP criterion
Jammu and Kashmir becoming a Union Territory
accepted.x: The reduction was attributed to Jammu and Kashmir becoming a Union Territory.
accepted.tq: Link the change in percentage to the specific institutional change responsible for it.

accepted.s: Which major change was associated with the 14th Finance Commission?
o: A shift towards tax devolution as the main route, along with ignoring the Plan/non-Plan distinction
A shift from tax devolution to exclusive grants
Introduction of the GDP criterion for the first time
accepted.x: The 14th Finance Commission made tax devolution the main route instead of grants and ignored the Plan/non-Plan distinction.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of policy change by contrasting devolution with grants.

accepted.s: Under the 14th Finance Commission’s allocation formula for local-body grants, the weights assigned to the 2011 population and area were respectively:

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the 16th Finance Commission:
1. It retained the States’ share at 41%.
2. It introduced a contribution to GDP criterion carrying a 10% weight.
3. It discontinued revenue-deficit grants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 16th Finance Commission retained 41%, introduced the GDP criterion with a 10% contribution and discontinued revenue-deficit grants.
accepted.tq: Combine percentage, criterion and grant-policy facts in one coded statement question.

accepted.s: What contribution to the criteria was assigned to the new GDP criterion by the 16th Finance Commission?
